study_identification_part.si_4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: HCP-Aging, HCP-Young Adult, and HCP-Development were used as the primary datasets for model construction. A clinical dataset from the Memory, Ageing & Cognition Centre (MACC) at the National University of Singapore (a single-site clinical cohort) was used for translational evaluation.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: This study uses three publicly available healthy brain imaging datasets that were provided and curated by the Human Connectome Project (HCP) 101 ; namely, HCP's Young Adult 102 , Aging 103 , and Development 104 cohorts. ... we evaluated the model's translational capabilities to real-world data from memory clinics (Memory, Ageing & Cognition Centre at the National University of Singapore: MACC)

answer.SINGLE-SITE: clinical evaluation (HC, MCI, AD) and transfer learning fine-tuning

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The three HCP cohorts were aggregated and split into 80% training and 20% test sets for normative model construction and validation. The MACC dataset (SINGLE-SITE) was used for independent clinical evaluation across healthy, MCI, and AD groups, with a subset of 66 HC used to fine-tune site-specific parameters via transfer learning.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: 80% ( N train =1978 individuals) of the healthy data were used to train the model, and the remaining 20% ( N test =495) were used for out-of-sample validation ... the normative model, pre-trained on N train healthy individuals, was subsequently fine-tuned for the clinical sample ... site parameters for dataset harmonization were fine-tuned on a subsample of 66 healthy individuals (50% of the HC cohort) from the MACC clinical cohort.
